note: The `error` codes the server can emit that the console does not branch on, and why. contract/error-codes.json is the server's half, rendered from internal/api's syntax tree; src/api/error-codes.ts is the console's. scripts/check-contract.mjs requires every served code to be in one set or the other, so this file is the only place a code may go unhandled — and it costs a name and a reason to put one here. A code that stops being served, or that the console starts handling, makes its exemption stale and fails the check: this list cannot rot quietly.

codes.reason: Emitted only on listeners the console never calls. The console speaks to the console listener alone (D19, and the mount table proves it) — the PEP surface belongs to workloads holding client credentials, and the callback surface to the IdP's redirect and to external systems pushing events. A code that cannot arrive is not a code to word, and wording one would be writing copy for a screen that can never render it.

Answered by the status rather than by the code. src/api/client.ts turns 401 into a re-login the shell offers, and reports the rest as the failure they are; none of the three says anything a screen would word differently from what the status already means — the session is gone, the engine is failing, the subsystem is not installed in this deployment.

The server's own sentence is the most accurate one available, and the console shows it. These refusals arrive on surfaces the console does call, and each carries a specific message written where the rule lives — which quorum is unsatisfiable, which floor a revision breaks, which capability is missing. A console-side rewording would be a second copy of that text, maintained apart from the rule it describes, and it would drift. The generic branch renders `message` verbatim, so nothing is lost by not naming these.

Recognised by its payload rather than by its code. The dry run answers a policy that will not decode with a `diagnostics` array of pointer/code/message triples, and the builder's job is to hang each one on the field that caused it — so what it keys off is the array, in src/builder/diagnostics.ts, and the code beside it adds nothing a screen would do differently. Worth writing down rather than leaving implicit: it is the one refusal on this API the console identifies by shape, and that is why the code looks unhandled when it is not.
